questions.question: Given `type ToArray<T> = T extends unknown ? T[] : never;`, what is `ToArray<string | number>`?
questions.explanation: T is a naked type parameter, so the conditional distributes over the union: ToArray<string> | ToArray<number>, which is string[] | number[]. Wrapping as [T] extends [unknown] would give (string | number)[].

questions.question: Given `type IsString<T> = T extends string ? "yes" : "no";`, what is `IsString<never>`?
questions.explanation: never is the empty union. A distributive conditional maps over each member, and there are none, so the result is never. Use [T] extends [never] to test for never.

questions.question: Which definition extracts the element type of an array type, returning T unchanged for non-arrays?
options: type El<T> = T extends (infer E)[] ? E : T;
type El<T> = T extends any[] ? T[number] : never;
type El<T> = infer E extends T[] ? E : T;
type El<T> = T[] extends infer E ? E : T;
questions.explanation: infer declares a type variable inside the extends clause. If T matches (infer E)[], E holds the element type; otherwise the false branch returns T. The second option returns never for non-arrays, and the other two are invalid or wrong.

questions.question: A function has two overloads: `(x: string): string` and `(x: number): number`. What does `ReturnType<typeof fn>` give?
questions.explanation: When inferring from an overloaded function type, conditional types use only the last overload signature, so the result is number.
